summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence, with history of gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer and reflux, presented with one week of dry heaving and epigastric pain similar to a recent admission. In the ED she was afebrile and hemodynamically stable without leukocytosis; labs including electrolytes, renal function, lactate, and lipase were reassuring and urinalysis was negative. She was admitted to the surgical ward for observation and treated with intravenous fluids including thiamine/folate/multivitamin, proton pump inhibitor therapy, symptom control with antiemetics and analgesia, and resumption of G-tube feeds (protein formula at 55 mL/hr), with resolution of symptoms and stable tolerance of enteral nutrition. She was discharged home ambulatory with continuation of home medications, addition of sucralfate, PRN oxycodone for pain, and outpatient follow-up with her surgeon.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Personal history of peptic ulcer disease
